short: Argentina has no AI law. Several member bills sit in the Chamber of Deputies, and the data protection authority, the AAIP, has issued non-binding AI guidance; Law 25.326 on personal data binds.
title: Argentina AI Laws
subtitle: No AI law: member bills in Congress and non-binding AAIP guidance
body_html:
Status at a glance

No AI act. Argentina has no AI law. Several bills by individual deputies are before the Chamber of Deputies, among them 2130-D-2025, a legal framework for the responsible development and use of AI systems that was on the Science, Technology and Productive Innovation committee's agenda on 16 September 2025, and a 2026 bill by Deputy Juan Fernando Brügge on the legal regime for the responsible use of AI. The Agency for Access to Public Information (AAIP) published a preliminary guide to using AI responsibly on 27 September 2024; it is not binding. Law 25.326 on the protection of personal data binds. Verified on 25 October 2026 against the Chamber of Deputies, InfoLEG and the AAIP.

Key instruments

InstrumentNumberDateStatus
Legal framework for the development, implementation and responsible use of AI systemsBill 2130-D-2025Committee agenda 16 September 2025Member bill
Legal regime for the responsible use of AI in Argentina2026 bill (Dep. Brügge)2026Member bill
Guide to using AI responsibly (preliminary)AAIP27 September 2024Non-binding guidance
Law on the protection of personal dataLey 25.326Sanctioned 4 October 2000In force

Who regulates and enforces

  • Agency for Access to Public Information (AAIP): data protection and AI guidance.
  • The 2026 Brügge bill would make the National Institute of Industrial Technology (INTI) the AI authority (art. 16); it is a proposal.

Scope and reach

No AI statute. The Brügge bill, as proposed, would cover providers, deployers, importers, distributors, manufacturers and users, and exclude research and development before market placement (art. 3).

Core obligations

  • None under an AI law. Law 25.326 governs AI that processes personal data.

Penalties

BreachMaximumProvisionEnforcer
Infringements of Law 25.326A fine of ARS 1,000 to ARS 100,000, with suspension or closure of the database; later regulatory scales were not checkedLey 25.326, art. 31AAIP
Under the 2026 Brügge bill, if enactedFines of 1 to 1,000 "Argentinos Oro" (art. 17)BillINTI, as proposed

What is coming next

Committee work on the AI bills; no date set. The Chamber's bill index is watched weekly.

The direction of travel, as reported

The national government does not want an AI law. President Milei wrote in the Financial Times in 2026 that Argentina should offer freedom from regulation to AI developers and aims to be, in his phrase, the fourth AI hub in the world, and the executive sent Congress a bill on companies operated by AI; the Argentine press reads the bill as a corporate-law measure rather than an AI statute. Against that, El Cronista counted nineteen AI bills in the Chamber of Deputies, all from members. They fall into two groups. Framework bills, including 2130-D-2025, the Brügge regime bill noted above, and a Senate bill S-0071/2025 of 5 March 2025, would create an AI authority and principles. Criminal bills would add deepfake offences to the Código Penal: one filed in 2026 inserts articles 139 ter and 129 bis; another, reported in July 2026, adds article 157 ter with two to four years' imprisonment for removing the notice that content was AI-generated; and a July 2026 bill led by Deputy Pamela Verasay amends the Civil and Commercial Code, the Penal Code and Law 26.485 on violence against women to cover AI-altered intimate images, and was sent to the General Legislation and Penal Legislation committees. None had a committee opinion when checked.

Courts and provinces have moved first. A July 2025 ruling of the Cámara de Apelaciones de Zárate-Campana held, as a Chamber bill records it, that generating sexual images of minors with AI is already an offence under article 128 of the Penal Code. The Province of Buenos Aires issued Decree 742/2026, signed by Governor Kicillof, setting a framework for AI use in the provincial administration with two implementing resolutions, which a startup-sector outlet described as the counterpoint to national deregulation; it binds the provincial state and its suppliers, not the private sector at large. The AAIP's work rests on Resolution 161/2023, which created its Programme on Transparency and Personal Data Protection in the Use of AI, the basis for the 2024 guide.

For a company the position is therefore: no federal AI duties, Law 25.326 fully in force, a growing chance of a deepfake offence being enacted in 2027, and provincial procurement rules if selling AI to Buenos Aires province.

Last verified

4 November 2026, against the sources above. The Milei column, the nineteen-bill count, the Verasay bill, the Zárate-Campana ruling and Decree 742/2026 are as the Argentine press and a Chamber bill's recitals report them; the decree was not read in the provincial bulletin. Not confirmed on an official source and therefore left out: a November 2025 committee opinion on 2130-D-2025, and an executive bill of May 2026.
